title: Adaptive Traffic Signal Control Using a Multi-Tier Analytical and Fuzzy Logic Approach
content: Urban intersections in rapidly growing cities frequently experience persistent oversat-uration, where fixed-time traffic signals cannot adapt to fluctuating arrivals or residual queue build-up. This study develops an adaptive fuzzy logic traffic signal controller for congestion-prone intersections in infrastructure-constrained urban environments. The controller uses a Mamdani-type inference system to relate arrival flow and queue length to green-time extension through a bounded nonlinear mapping. The research integrates three modelling stages: baseline performance is evaluated using Highway Capacity Manual (HCM 2022) procedures, validated with SIDRA Intersection simulation, and the adaptive controller is tested in a closed-loop MATLAB/Simulink environment. Perfor-mance is assessed through 30 Monte Carlo simulations under peak oversaturated con-ditions. Compared with fixed-time control, the proposed controller reduces average control delay by more than 35% (p < 0.01), decreases the 95th percentile queue length, and improves throughput stability. Time-series analysis shows that the controller adjusts service rates in response to changing demand, limiting persistent queue growth. Sensi-tivity analysis further demonstrates stable performance under reasonable variations in traffic demand and parameter values. The findings indicate that fuzzy logic control of-fers an effective and practical adaptive traffic signal strategy for congested intersections, particularly in cities with limited advanced traffic management infrastructure.
